efren_mgr: Heads up  were consolidating two small infra teams and want to promote one IC to Senior Infra Eng as part of the lateral transfer. This will change their budget code across two cost centers (SRE + Platform). Director approved title and comp. What do we need to do for a cross-cost-center promotion + transfer?

lina_hr: Congrats. Two main threads: (A) HR paperwork for transfer + promotion, (B) Finance routing for cost-split. Submit a Role Change packet and in comments add: 'consolidation transfer, cost-split required (SRE:60%/Platform:40%)'. Attach director approval and consolidation memo.

jaya_finance: For cost-splits we need a signed finance approval from both cost owners. Provide the % split and the GL codes. Also indicate which org owns the headcount after transfer (one owner must be primary for budgeting). We can apportion salary and run amortization for partial months.

meera_comp: Comp note: because this is a lateral transfer + title bump, we'll check band alignment. If the proposed base is within target band we can approve with manager + director evidence. If it crosses band or is >10% above midpoint, we'll escalate to Comp Review Board. For board, we need manager rationale, market comps, deliverables, and director memo.

efren_mgr: OK. We're proposing +8% base, same band. Will that avoid the board? Also employee is relocating offices (SF->NY) with a relocation allowance request.

meera_comp: +8% within same band typically OK; provide 3 bullets for scope increase and two measurable outcomes. Relocation is separate: submit Comp Adjustment for one-time relocation payment, include amount and pay period. Relocation doesn't change base.

jaya_finance: Relocation paid as one-time expense. For cross-cost-center charge we need to confirm which cost center pays the relocation. If you want to split relocation cost, state split in the Comp Adj form. Finance also needs to know currency (USD) and payment method.

michael_payroll: Payroll operationally: to have title + base change effective 2026-01-01 without retro, final approved Role Change packet must hit payroll inbox by 2025-12-18 EOD. Relocation one-time payments need separate Comp Adj filed at least 5 business days before preferred pay date. Include employee ID and preferred pay period.

efren_mgr: If both cost centers approve but finance needs headcount ownership decided post-facto, can we set primary now and reallocate later?

jaya_finance: You can set a primary cost owner now to process payroll. If allocation changes later we will do a journal entry to reclassify expenses, but that creates manual work. Best to finalize splits now.

lina_hr: Quick checklist for you @efren_mgr: 1) Role Change packet (choose 'transfer + title change'), 2) attach consolidation memo, director approval, and cost-split approval emails, 3) Comp Adj for relocation with cost-split note, 4) call out primary cost owner, 5) ping payroll when submitted.

efren_mgr: Thanks. One last: can we backdate effective to 2025-12-01 to align with org restructure announcement?

meera_comp: Backdating will cause retro if approvals miss payroll cutoff. If you must show internal announcement 12/1, consider title-only effective 12/01 in HRIS (no pay change) and base change effective 2026-01-01. Note that title-only may affect calibration; document in the packet.

michael_payroll: Agreed. Title-only entries are fine for org chart messaging. Any base change effective earlier requires final approvals by payroll cutoff to avoid retro.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: Required Role Change fields: employee name, employee ID, current title, new title, proposed base (or note 'title-only'), effective date(s), manager rationale, director approval, budget code(s) and % split if needed, attachments allowed (PDF or Drive link). HR portal: https://hr.redwood.internal/role-change. Finance guide: https://finance.redwood.internal/cost-split. Payroll deadlines: https://payroll.redwood.internal/deadlines.
